If you're willing to wait a little while and don't need to grab the latest Apple product on launch day, Apple's official refurbished store has always been an excellent choice. Typically around three months after a new product launches, the first refurbished models start appearing on Apple's website.

Other companies also offer their own options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but it's important to understand the different standards and warranty terms that apply…

Apple Certified Refurbished

Purchasing from Apple's certified refurbished store typically gets you around a 15% discount, and the products themselves are indistinguishable from brand new ones. Specifically, Apple guarantees all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing performed by Apple
  • Brand new housing with absolutely no scratches or wear
  • Brand new battery, ensuring battery life is the same as a regular product
  • All original accessories and cables included
  • Eligible for Apple's standard one-year warranty, exactly the same as a brand new product
  • Also eligible to purchase AppleCare+

Basically, the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box rather than the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed is typically priced more competitively, but it's worth noting that you don't get the same assurances when it comes to product condition:

  • Inspected and tested by the seller, not Apple
  • Uses previous housing, with scratches and wear expected (see below)
  • Uses a previous battery, only guaranteed to maintain at least 80% of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be genuine Apple
  • Comes with a 90-day Amazon warranty instead of Apple's one-year warranty

As for scratches and wear, Amazon offers three quality grades:

  • Premium / Excellent: No visible cosmetic flaws when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: Light scratches that are barely noticeable when viewed from 12 inches away from the device
  • Acceptable: Scratches that are clearly visible and can be felt to the touch

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is far vaguer than Amazon in describing what you'll get:

  • No guarantee on cosmetic condition, only a promise of "like-new performance and reliability"
  • No specific mention of battery condition beyond what's noted above
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller rather than Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair tiers come with 90 days. The company doesn't clearly define what each tier means.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want a product that matches a brand new one in both condition and Apple warranty coverage, then Apple's refurbished store is clearly the top choice.

That said, Amazon Renewed's pricing is clearly more competitive, so if you're willing to accept the trade-offs noted above, it could be considered a pretty good deal. Especially if you're planning to follow our advice and save money by upgrading to an iPhone 17 Pro rather than this year's model (since you'd only be sacrificing one cable), there are some pretty attractive deals:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (originally $1,499 new) — all-time low
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (originally $1,499 new) — all-time low
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (originally $1,499 new) — all-time low
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (originally $1,299 new) — all-time low
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (originally $1,299 new) — all-time low
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (originally $1,299 new) — just $1 off all-time low

As for Walmart Restored, I'd be concerned about the extremely vague promises, but if you're not satisfied, you can always return it.
